content.user_title: Check Taiwan Power Supply and Reserve Capacity
content.value_statement: Taiwan power supply reports combine current readings and forecasts that can be difficult to interpret. This skill retrieves Taipower open data and summarizes load, reserves, supply indicators, and publication time.
actual_capabilities: Guide retrieval of public Taipower supply and demand JSON without an API key or login.
Identify current load and utilization fields in the response.
Report forecast maximum supply, peak demand, reserve capacity, and reserve percentage.
Interpret the documented green, yellow, orange, red, and black supply indicators.
Read yesterday's actual results and real-time peak records.
Explain ROC calendar timestamps, power unit conversion, and retrieval failure handling.
limitations: Requires network access and an available Taipower open data endpoint.
Does not provide regional rationing lists, local outage schedules, or individual electricity account readings.
Forecast reserves and supply indicators do not guarantee uninterrupted service at a specific location.
Records can mix dates near midnight; data freshness depends on the source publication time.

use_cases.title: Check the latest supply status
use_cases.description: Review current electricity demand, forecast reserves, and the published supply indicator before discussing national power conditions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a power supply brief
use_cases.description: Summarize current readings and forecasts with clear timestamps and units for a factual energy news update.

use_cases.title: Review daily grid conditions
use_cases.description: Compare today's forecast with yesterday's actual peak while keeping forecast and observed values distinct.

prompt_templates.title: Basic supply check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Taiwan's latest power supply indicator and reserve percentage. Include the source publication time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: obtain a short status report.

prompt_templates.title: Demand and forecast summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Report current load, utilization, forecast maximum supply, peak demand, and reserve capacity. Keep the original units and include publication time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review the main supply and demand metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Compare daily records
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare today's forecast peak with yesterday's actual peak. Identify each record's date and distinguish forecasts from observed values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare forecast and actual records.

prompt_templates.title: Check interpretation and freshness
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the latest Taipower data. Check response success, publication dates, and mixed-day records. Convert power values to MW and explain the supply indicator.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review response interpretation and unit consistency.

output_examples.input: Report the status when the Taipower data request fails repeatedly.
output_examples.output: The Taipower data source is unavailable. Current demand, reserve capacity, and supply status cannot be verified from this request.

best_practices: Include the source publication time and distinguish today's forecast from observed readings.
Preserve original units or explicitly convert each unit of 10,000 kW to 10 MW.
Use the documented open data host and report persistent retrieval failures without inventing values.
anti_patterns: Presenting historical examples or stale records as current power conditions.
Treating a national reserve indicator as a confirmed local outage or rationing schedule.
Combining midnight records without checking dates or mixing forecast values with actual readings.

faq.question: Do I need an API key or account?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses a public Taipower open data endpoint without authentication.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Live retrieval requires network access and a suitable request tool.

faq.question: Can this skill check my electricity account or local outage?
faq.answer: No. It covers national supply and demand records, not individual accounts, regional rationing lists, or local outage schedules.

faq.question: What does the supply indicator mean?
faq.answer: Green means ample supply; yellow means tight supply; orange means a supply alert. Red and black indicate escalating rationing warnings.

faq.question: How are dates and power units handled?
faq.answer: Publication time uses the ROC calendar, while real-time peak time uses Gregorian dates. One unit of 10,000 kW equals 10 MW.

faq.question: What happens when the data endpoint fails?
faq.answer: The skill recommends retrying with a browser user agent. Persistent failures should be reported as source errors without fabricated reserve figures.
